user_summary_md:
## Your Situation

You are 24 years old, just starting your career in the US, with **$300/month** to invest toward long-term wealth building. You have no existing investments — which is actually a great position to be in.

Current macro: CPI at 3.2%, Fed funds rate at 5.25%, S&P 500 returned +24% YTD at a P/E of 28 (1.3σ above 10-year average of 21). Macro environment is moderately favourable for equity index investing.
portfolio_diagnosis_md: You currently hold no investments. Cash savings are safe short-term, but inflation (currently 3.2%) erodes purchasing power over long horizons. Financial readiness: solid — you have monthly surplus and a clear goal. Starting now with $300/month compounds significantly over 10+ years via dollar-cost averaging.

options.title: Conservative Beginner Plan
options.best_for: Users nervous about early market losses
options.content_md:
### Asset Allocation
| Asset | Allocation | Monthly |
|---|---|---|
| Emergency fund (HYSA) | 40% | $120 |
| Broad index fund (VOO, 0.03% expense ratio) | 40% | $120 |
| Short-term bond fund | 20% | $60 |

### Why this works
Dollar-cost averaging into a diversified equity index. Emergency buffer first.

### Pros
- Low emotional stress
- Builds emergency buffer first
- Ultra-low cost (0.03%/yr)

### Cons
- Slower wealth creation vs. full equity

### Agent guidance
Choose this if your biggest fear is losing money in the first 6–12 months.

| Total market index (VTI, 0.03% ER) | 90% | $270 |
| Cash reserve | 10% | $30 |

### Why this works
Full equity exposure maximises long-term compound returns. VTI 10y CAGR: ~12%.

### Pros
- Highest long-term expected return
- Extremely low cost

### Cons
- High volatility; 2008 drawdown: -52%

### Agent guidance
Only if a 30% paper loss won't cause you to sell.

hidden_disclosures: VOO expense ratio: 0.03%/yr (~$0.90/yr per $3,000 invested) — extremely low.
FXAIX expense ratio: 0.015%/yr — Fidelity's zero-minimum fund, lowest in class.
Short-term capital gains tax applies if any position sold within 12 months (up to 37% in US).
Past performance does not guarantee future returns.
